next.text: ## Open Design Questions Under This Vision
next.sectionText:
## Open Design Questions Under This Vision

The earlier questions now have mixed status; answered contracts and still-open designs must be distinguished:

- Inline schema is now answered by the current validator; its reserved mutation
  stamp gate is distinct from the Unit-run mutating worktree/binding gate.
- Current declared/inline provenance and normalization are answered by the
  Assignment builder/normalizer; a broader dynamic graph remains a proposal.
- Additional unlike consumers must still prove new generic extension seams.
- Provider privacy/context-egress guarantees need evidence from the effective
  governance/confinement path; future soul/provider policies are not implied.
- General same-workspace inherited-edit takeover remains an unimplemented
  recovery profile, not an existing session-isolation mechanism.
- Nested Work integration topology remains a separate owning-domain decision.

The earlier V-003/V-009 session graph formulations remain historical. The
desired breadth of a future generic dynamic graph is open, not asserted shipped.

These belong in proposals, ADRs, architecture, and contracts beneath this
Vision. They must be answered without reopening V-001 through V-013 implicitly.

## Reading Down From The Vision

1. [Vocabulary](vocabulary/README.md) names current, proposed and reserved terms.
2. [Architecture](architecture/README.md) routes to current implementation owners
   and explicitly proposed designs.
3. [Assignment, Run and RunResult contract](contracts/assignment-run-runresult.md)
   distinguishes current execution/evidence boundaries from historical schemas.
4. [Decisions](decisions/README.md) distinguishes surviving boundaries from
   retired-engine acceptance.
5. [Historical Step 07](history/retired-engine/files/proposals/step-07-coordination-session-adhoc-task.md#literal-snapshot)
   and [Step 08](history/retired-engine/files/proposals/step-08-standalone-coordination-protocols.md#literal-snapshot)
   preserve their earlier frontier; they do not define current execution doors.
6. Current sequencing and binding implementation is linked by
   [the runner spec](../runner/spec.md). The two recorded spec/code conflicts
   require separate main-owner investigation, not inference from old acceptance.

previous.text: Fallback (Provider Capacity, tầng 1) từng chọn invocation MẶC ĐỊNH của candidate fallback một cách mù — khi 1 executor mang nhiều invocation khác `confinement` (executor-id-consolidation), phép chọn mù đó có thể lặng lẽ hạ cấp 1 primary có confinement xuống 1 fallback KHÔNG confinement. `selectConfinedInvocationId` (`resolve.mjs`) đóng gap này: kiểm CẤU TRÚC thuần ("candidate có invocation nào khai confinement không"), không bao giờ kiểm ngữ nghĩa policy (việc đó vẫn thuộc Confinement Authority, `confinement/authority.mjs`, không đụng tới) — primary có confinement mà fallback không tìm được invocation nào có confinement thì bị refuse thẳng, không âm thầm dispatch hở. Phạm vi CHỈ áp cho đường fallback provider-capacity; đường redirect read-only (RUL trên/Phase D) là cơ chế khác, không đụng tới ở đây. `opPolicy.fallbackExecutors` giữ nguyên `string[]` — không mở rộng thành `{executor, invocation}` (việc đó phải chạm 8+ file ở tầng khai báo Workflow/Operation, không cần thiết khi bản check cấu trúc trên đã đóng đúng gap thật).

Gọi từ bên trong `approve` nguồn `runner` (Cổng duyệt PR nội bộ), ngay trước bước kiểm cây sạch, cho MỌI đề xuất nguồn runner đang land LÊN TRUNK (thu hẹp về ranh giới trunk per `0032`) — xem "Cổng duyệt PR nội bộ" và "Iron Law" dưới, Business Rules RUL36 (`evolve --submit` là hành động ghi duy nhất trên bề mặt evolve, tái dùng chính cửa `submit`)/RUL37 (Iron Law hỏi ở đúng một ranh giới — trunk — cho mọi đề xuất nguồn runner tới đó)/RUL64 (`ironLaw.level` — key config riêng của cổng Iron Law, fail-closed về `ask`) | required (có/không cần chứng minh test-đỏ-trước), matchedFlags (danh sách từ khóa rủi ro nặng khớp trong mô tả fix), matchedModules (danh sách file khớp danh sách module minh họa) | — | required mặc định `false` khi cả hai phép thử đều không khớp |

next.sectionText:
### Hợp đồng rigor và tier (cập nhật 2026-10-21)

Workflow/Unit và operation phát biểu nhu cầu bằng `rigor = low|standard|high|critical`. `rigor` gộp chỉ-nâng qua workflow → unit → assignment, rồi gộp với `capabilities.<cap>.rigor`; nó chỉ quyết số checker của một unit `reviewed` và mức độc lập giữa các ghế, **không** quyết tier và không đặt mức effort. Tier của một ghế agent được khai trực tiếp trong config và giải theo thứ tự ưu tiên của [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md) mục 6.3; model chọn tại `runner.modelPolicies[family][tier]`. Việc chọn tier, model, effort, thứ tự executor, thứ tự account và bước fallback cho ghế agent do Seat Binding làm authority (D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice)); `bind()` trong Execution Core là facade mỏng của nó. Trần `runner.maxTier` hạ tier một cách hiển thị (`max-tier-cap`); `--tier` và các cửa chọn khác nâng tier bị từ chối theo mục 5.5 của spec đó.

**Effort và model khi launch.** Effort lấy từ cell của tier, từ `--effort` (không được thấp hơn cell), hoặc mặc định của invocation; `rigor` không đặt effort. Một mức nêu tường minh được render vào lệnh chạy ở một chỗ, `resolveExecutorCommand`, theo CLI được spawn (`provider-adapter.mjs` `renderReasoningEffortArgs`): claude/agy `--effort`, pi/omp `--thinking` (thay giá trị template đã ghi cứng), codex `-c model_reasoning_effort=` (`max` → `xhigh`); CLI không có điều khiển effort → từ chối trước khi spawn.

Model chạy lệch với model đã bind được ghi thành provenance: receipt `assignment-run-result` mang `policy.provenance.modelDrift = {value: [...], source}` và `policy.provenance.reasoningEffort.rendered` (cờ thật đã render). Mã cảnh báo: `model-overridden` (policy thay model trước launch, vd redirect sang provider khác tính lại theo tier), `model-not-passed` (argv không chứa model), `model-unsupported` (CLI từ chối/không biết model — câu từ chối thật của agy, pi, codex), `model-reported-different` (header `model:` trên stderr của codex khác model đã truyền). Kiểm trước-spawn ở `resolveExecutorCommand` (`modelCheck`), sau-run ở `collectModelWarnings`, cả hai trong `provider-adapter.mjs`, dùng chung cho mọi cửa; kết quả `execute` thô (compat) mang cùng dữ liệu ở `reasoningEffort`/`modelWarnings`.

Capability được khai `tier` và `maxTier` của chính nó, cùng `roles`, `personas` và `seats` (khẩu vị theo vai, persona và ghế). Config còn `runner.rigorToTier`, `capabilities.*.overrides`, bảng model phẳng, hoặc field quality bridge cũ bị từ chối với hướng dẫn chạy `fgos setup`; setup/doctor sở hữu việc chuyển đổi (có backup) và chẩn đoán.

| Component | Current role | Current source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
| Workflow (guide + case; `src/workflow/**`) | Component Workflow with two entities, guide and case (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), partially supersedes 0048 §2 and 0049 §4; behaviour per [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), implementation follows its plan). Human review gates. A consumer of Git's Land and Sync; owns no git mutation of its own. Single authority for the guide schema and its pinned snapshot per case; the case ledger (approved frame, reservations, route/deviation events, gate answers bound to subject digests, receipts, milestone projection, close); admission (is a proposed activity lawful now, against a closed catalog of machine checks); the worktree binding record (keyed by worktree root identity, with a generation) and the frame counters. Implements the AdmissionPort that Execution Core declares; imports flow Workflow → Execution Core only. Chooses no order: the agent proposes, the case admits and records; the Playbook proposer proposes through admission like any agent. Admission predicates, projection and the port implementation sit at infra or lower; the Playbook proposer at use-case. The ledger stays the JSONL under `advance`, hardened in place (fsync before release, reader fails closed); not an Event Store consumer in this cutover (owner 2026-10-19). Consumer of Execution Core and Git. Never owns who/model/persona, verify execution, locks, writer identity, merge or Work status. | [../specs/workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Execution Core (Unit, Unit run, `bind()`, Pattern cộng tác, cửa `fgos run`, posture) | Single authority for how a Unit runs (mechanism, posture, gates), through a single run door for new work (`fgos run` via `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`, herdr pane default, cli fallback), OS confinement posture for both herdr and cli, verifiable mutating gate. Strictly forbids L3 Work lifecycle dependencies (`src/state/**`). Owns the AdmissionPort interface (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)) (resolve the target worktree's binding, admit, settle), never the admission decision; every `runUnit` caller with writes (the run door, the Playbook proposer and the Work paths running today) injects Workflow's real implementation from the day it lands, and the port accepts an `advance` hold the caller already has. `runUnit` refuses a mutating Unit with no port, and a standalone write passes only on an affirmative `unbound`. The door resolves the caller's authority context conjunctively after pattern resolution and before `bind()`; the port stays present at the mutating gate, which re-checks subject-bound consent at effect; the door sets the case context in the worker's launch env and strips any inherited one. A nested writing dispatch from a confined worker is refused by name (owner 2026-10-19). It no longer chooses a seat: which executor, model, effort, tier and account an agent seat gets, and where it goes on failure, belongs to Seat Binding (next row, D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding)); `src/runner/execution/bind.mjs` is the thin facade that collects machine facts and asks it. Persona files are loaded by `agent-definitions` (names and paths by Convention). | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Seat Binding (`fgos-seat-binding`) | Single authority for "which executor, invocation, model, effort, tier and account runs this agent seat, and where it goes on failure", with the reason for each part ([spec §3](../specs/seat-binding.md)). Two pure stages in a Rust crate (static policy, then ranking) behind the internal route `fgos internal seat-binding bind\|ladder`; thin Node client `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` (fails closed; inside an activated release the activation host answers). Depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. Agent seats only: a capability served by a tool executor keeps its own path. Account state (lease, release, quarantine, probe) is reached through the provider-capacity port: the facade reads the account view outside the provider lock, and the lease takes exactly the account the crate named; no host exec runs under that lock. Owns the tier ladder (the source of the config `$comment`). Does not own the seat list (the seat resolver, from pattern and workflow `seats:`), launching, transport, confinement, admission or persona loading. | [../specs/seat-binding.md](../specs/seat-binding.md), `packages/seat-binding/rust`, `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` |
| Collaboration Patterns (Execution Core) | Domain-neutral small collaboration loops (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`) and presets (`consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`). Replaces retired coordination engine. | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Herdr (Transport chính + Bề mặt quan sát) | Transport mặc định cho out-of-process runs, pane execution liveness, plugin `herdr-dashboard/` (TUI trong pane herdr + pick/pane supervisor; herdr nạp qua `herdr-plugin.toml`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| fgos Gateway | Tiến trình detached duy nhất phục vụ REST API (`/v1`, hợp đồng CTR010), MCP `search`/`execute` trên cùng cổng, và bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn (`apps/fgos-gateway/`: `gateway.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `cf_access.rs`, `remote_invocation.rs`, `web/`). Vòng đời duy nhất qua `fgos gateway start\|status\|stop`; không phải một phần của herdr và không phải "herdr-gateway" (tên đó chỉ repo tham chiếu ngoài). Dùng chung với `herdr-dashboard` lớp adapter CLI fgos tại `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` (`fgos.rs`, `settings.rs`, trait `WorkItemSource`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [../specs/confinement-authority.md](../specs/confinement-authority.md) |
| Run Result Evaluator | Evidence/confidence boundary for assignment run results. | [../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md](../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md) |
| Domain Components And Extension Layer | Domain-specific behavior, workflows, skills, task specs, doctrine. L2 prose no longer picks executors or mechanisms (lớp matching L2 cũ đã thu hồi per 0048); thin driver `fgos-run` delegates directly to the Workflow door (`fgos workflow start`) and P1 Execution Core (`fgos run`); a conductor names the Workflow case on each dispatch. | [../../domains/](../../domains/), [../architect/domainization/](../architect/domainization/) |
| Host And Surface Layer | CLI, fgos Gateway (REST/MCP/web), `herdr-dashboard` plugin and other Herdr surfaces into platform engines. | Host invocation and gateway docs |
| Packaging-Distribution | Runtime packaging, install, activation, setup/doctor readiness. | [packaging-distribution/README.md](packaging-distribution/README.md) |
| Knowledge, Learning, And Documentation Registry | Retrospective learning, doc registry, end-user docs index, trace/evolve signals. | Knowledge and docs registry docs |
| Observe (Metrics & Friction) | Measurement and friction tracking across substrate entities (cases, runs, sessions, friction, snapshots). Owned in Rust (`packages/observe/rust`), native routing. | [../specs/observe.md](../specs/observe.md) |
| Convention (Executable Names & Placement) | Platform-core authority for deterministic artifact names, repository-relative placement, path classification, and conformance checking. Implemented; owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. | [convention/spec.md](convention/spec.md) |
| Identity (foundation; today the local session writer id) | Foundation authority for identities, today for "who is the writer of this process" (`{id, source}`). One implementation, the Rust crate `fgos-identity` (`packages/identity/rust`, native verb `fgos identity`); Observe calls it in process, Node through the facade `src/util/session-identity.mjs` over the combined addon's `sessionIdentity` namespace. Also mints the writer id of an attempt (`att-<attemptId>`) and carries the launcher's env scrub the gate applies. Also mints and reads the machine id (`<stateRoot>/machine-id`, optional `machine-alias`; `fgos identity machine`, doctor row `identity-machine-id`) and derives the machine handle; also reads and, on an explicit `fgos identity project --init`, mints the project id (the tracked file `.fgos/project.json`; doctor row `identity-project-id`; the provider reads the Git component for the trusted main root and the remote default branch); the one validator of the id shape lives here. The host provider sits behind the default cargo feature `provider` (needs `fgos-host-runtime`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-convention`, `fgos-git`); Event Store and the node addon depend on the library with `default-features = false`, so the event log never pulls the host runtime. The process-tree adapter reads `/proc` through `fgos-process` (a plain dependency, an L0 leaf, not behind `provider`). Observe depends on it; the run supervisor's controller half calls the mint and, through the library without `provider`, the ISO-8601 UTC clock `text::iso_utc_now` (host-runtime's `civil_time` stays the clock of the crates that already sit on the host runtime; it cannot call identity, whose provider depends on it). The machine-id mint reaches Node through the addon's `sessionIdentity.mintMachineId`, wrapped by `src/util/identity-mint.mjs`. Grants no lock or claim authority. | [identity/spec.md](identity/spec.md) |
| Terminal-control (L2) | Foundation component for "which pane does this key run in" on a terminal multiplexer, usable without a run. Rust crate `fgos-terminal-control` (`packages/terminal-control/rust`) with a key-addressed upper port and a driver port with declared capabilities (herdr first; Windows declares none). Writes only the allocation record; closes only panes it allocated, never a tab; Node reaches it through the internal route `fgos internal terminal-control`, no user verb. Dependency one way: run supervisor → Terminal-control (the supervisor holds the key, the attempt id, never a pane). Node migration done; setup adds the `terminal` config section and `<stateRoot>/terminal`, doctor runs `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. | [terminal-control/spec.md](terminal-control/spec.md) |
| Process Facts & Control (L0) | Single authority for "is this process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}` alive, dead or unknown" (`judge`, one vector file run by cargo), for signalling a process by identity (`pidfd` on Linux, never a bare pid), for spawning with an explicit fd mapping, and for the domain primitives `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs. Never spawns to read facts, never kills by bare pid, never reads mtime, knows no run, lock or pane. Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), one driver per OS; Node reaches it only through the in-process door (`src/native/door.mjs` → `src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs`, six exports, at most 60 lines, no `/proc`, no `process.kill`); reconcile imports the thin client. Callers reclaim only on `dead` and count a process stopped only after a `sent` signal and a `dead` judgement; `unknown` always holds. Loader errors `process-door-unavailable` and `process-door-not-shipped` fail closed with a next step. No Node file judges a recorded process or signals a bare pid: the only `process.kill` calls left signal the process group of a child the same code just spawned, and the remaining `/proc` readers (lock-holder fd scan, doctor checks, confinement probes) are listed with their reasons in `test/process/one-door.test.mjs`, which fails on any other site. The doctor row kept is `process-containment`. The gate primitives (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) stay with the run supervisor; the containment port lives in this crate (row below). Depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md) |
| Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank and path), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule and the single state-root resolution. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the `holderLock` namespace of the combined addon, which the facade takes once through a one-shot capability (Node runs every lock operation in process on Linux and macOS), and the four surviving internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd` (borrowed check and shared try, for the git hook), `lock-hold` (Windows), `quiesce-scan` and `lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. The state root is the host's pin, else the door's `holderLock.stateRoot`; the checkout channel `node bin/fgos.mjs` is unsupported for lock verbs. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. The `linux-pgroup` driver sets no subreaper on its caller and answers `is_empty` `unknown`, never `empty`, when a seen or listed member cannot be judged or read. Node has no caller of `create`, `spawn_in`, `guarantee` or the domain calls, so the addon exports none of them. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Durable file (L0 leaf) | Single authority for how an fgOS record reaches disk when its loss must not go unnoticed: temp file, fsync of the file, install (replace, or create-only without replacing), fsync of the directory; every error says the step it failed at and which effect already happened (`installed: created \| already-exists \| none`); the file mode is explicit, and an omitted or invalid mode is refused by name (`durable-file-mode-invalid`) before anything is written. A create-only writer that finds the name already there leaves without a directory fsync. Rust crate `fgos-durable-file` (`packages/durable-file/rust`); Node through the door exports `replaceDurably` and `installOnce` in `src/native/door.mjs`, which remove the retained temporary on failure. Node keeps its per-module no-fsync helpers (no shared write helper), each naming its temporary with `uniqueTmpTag()`; the mode-preserving trust store, copy-then-rename and Work-owned writes stay. Accepted duplication: the private temp-then-rename helpers of the run supervisor (`supervise.rs`, `adopt.rs`, `supervise/windows.rs`) and holder-lock (`route/hold.rs`, `predecessor.rs`) do not fsync, because a heartbeat fsync on every tick would add I/O to every live run. Node budget: the Node replace and create-only helpers that already fsynced are deleted (target Node −110). Depends only on the OS. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| Canonical JSON (L0 leaf) | Single authority for the bytes of canonical JSON: RFC 8785 member order by UTF-16 code units and ECMAScript number text; input that is not JSON is refused by name. Rust crate `fgos-canonical-json` (`packages/canonical-json/rust`, `canonical_json`, `canonical_line`), vectors in `packages/canonical-json/contracts/vectors/`; Node through the door export `canonicalJson(value)` (`src/native/door.mjs`), which serialises with `JSON.stringify` (so a `Date` becomes its `toJSON` text) and hands the text to Rust, and refuses a hole, a non-finite number or a value `JSON.stringify` cannot serialise with `canonical-json-not-json` and drops an `undefined` member as `JSON.stringify` does. Node budget: one re-export line. Accepted exceptions, each with its reason: `recovery-planner.mjs` keeps its own `stableStringify` (its module contract is purity, its import set is pinned to `node:crypto`, and its stored records hold only hash outputs); `effective-execution-contract.mjs` and the release-manifest producer and verifier pair stay together until the Packaging plan moves them as one; `trust-store.mjs` `sortedJson` stays because it must match codex's own byte order, not RFC 8785. Depends only on `serde_json` and `ryu-js`. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| YAML Document (L0 leaf; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate and Rust consumers done, Node door not started) | Single authority for reading, editing and merging YAML text: a lossless document with semantic value and positions, two parse profiles (`strict-config` for config files, `tool` for workflows, personas, units and manifests, the latter keeping today's js-yaml door contract), edits that keep every untouched byte, comment blocks as positioned text with an injection guard, and a merge primitive whose per-path rules the caller supplies. Knows no config key, file scope, default, lock or comment grammar. Rust crate `fgos-yaml-doc` (planned `packages/yaml-doc/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `yaml` behind the kept facade `src/util/yaml.mjs`; replaces the vendored js-yaml (RUL101 superseded when it lands); `frontmatter.mjs` and `distill.mjs` stay on their own paths. Depends only on its parser crate. | [yaml-document/spec.md](yaml-document/spec.md) |
| Config (L1; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate, section schemas and standard done, not yet wired to any caller) | Single authority for fgOS configuration: which files are config (project `.fgos/config.yaml` over global `~/.fgos/config.yaml` over the read-only standard shipped with the release; config files hold only differences; account pools and the gateway token under `~/.fgos/private/`, hidden from confined workers), the schema dialect and engine (descriptors are data shipped by each section's owner under `core/config-schema/`), the effective snapshot with provenance, the three write doors (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `fgos config`) and their one-file transaction (new locks `project-config` and `global-config`, compare-and-swap on byte revision, Durable File replace), the `@fgos:doc` / `@fgos:why` comment grammar and when a reason is required, the config doctor checks and JSON-to-YAML migration. Reads never write. Never owns YAML syntax (YAML Document), lock mechanism (Holder-lock), secret values (Secrets), section meaning or cross-field rules (each section owner), or bootstrap JSON files. Rust crate `fgos-config` (planned `packages/config/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `config`, replacing `src/config/` and every direct reader. Depends on YAML Document, Holder-lock, Durable File and Secrets; acquires its own locks without reading config. | [config/spec.md](config/spec.md) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Its Publication port is the only door to `refs/fgos/*`, and Event Store is the only production writer of event refs through it. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon (`packages/git/node-addon`) that also links `fgos-event-store`, via the facade `src/git/`. Implemented through Git phase 07 (callers moved onto the typed ports); the whole-product one-door gate (`git-mutation-one-door`, spec §12) and the phase 08 proofs land with the Git plan's final release. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store (foundation) | Single authority for how an fgOS event becomes durable, is sealed into git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/*`, is shared across machines and is read back: the v4 envelope and stream registry, the per-stream open logs and their `event-append`/`event-seal` locks, seal and recovery, the reader with coverage, causal order and cursor, sync, and the store side of the `fgos events` verbs (`src/verbs/events/`). Planned consumers: Work, porting, observe, decisions; each owns its types, gate, reducer and view, and the store imports none of them (`packages/event-store/contracts/consumers.v1.json` is the only registry). Depends on Git's Publication port (the only door to `refs/fgos/*`), Holder-lock and Session Identity. Rust crate `fgos-event-store` (`packages/event-store/rust`); Node only through the facade `src/event-store/` over the one combined N-API addon shared with `fgos-git`. Dormant on main: store layer proven (2026-10-20), no consumer registered; the Work cutover is the WORK lane. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |
| Agent Mailbox (L4, signed at G0 on 2026-10-20; implementation not started) | Single authority for "how a message from one agent session is placed into the context of the right live head of a CLI on this machine, with an honest delivery report, and never as the user's input": the envelope, the delivery state machine (`recorded`, `in-flight`, `offered`, `refused`), the registry of heads (name, per-process generation, process `Record`), the channel-protection policies, the peer frame, and the per-CLI hook payload shape and non-terminal wake channels (the Claude Code scoped socket, `codex queue`). Recipients are independently started interactive heads, never a runner Unit attempt, a subagent or a teammate. Owns one runtime-state record per project at the main checkout's `.fgos` (not event truth, never replayed, never pushed). First slice imports only `fgos-process`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-durable-file` and `fgos-identity`; its core crate `fgos-mailbox-core` depends on serde alone. Never owns writer identity (Session Identity), process liveness (Process Facts & Control), the main-checkout `.fgos` resolver (the host), pane access (Terminal-control), typing or screen reading (Agent protocol; a later part), hook installation (the setup installer), locks (Holder-lock), communication authorization or case budgets (coordination foundation), or steering a Unit attempt (the runner). Rust crates `fgos-mailbox-core` and `fgos-mailbox` (planned: `packages/mailbox/rust`). | [agent-mailbox/spec.md](agent-mailbox/spec.md) |

1. `credentialStore: { use: <codex | pi | omp>, homeEnv: <CODEX_HOME | PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR>, files?: [...] }` trên invocation (cùng dạng `codex-cli-bwrap`; runner.md RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). Config viết trước field này (config toàn máy, project khác) vẫn khai `resourceBindings: [{ resource: 'private-home', target: { kind: 'env', name: <biến> } }]`; một hàm (`credentialStoreOf`) suy `credentialStore` từ đó, và nhánh suy này bị xoá khi các config ấy đã chuyển.
2. Login của account đến từ inventory toàn máy `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts.<id>.credentialSource` trong `~/.fgos/config.json` (RUL65b của `docs/specs/runner.md`): kind `codex-home` (`auth.json`) hoặc `home-files` (danh sách file tường minh, copy owner-only, fail closed) — driver `drivers/bwrap.mjs` copy vào private home trước khi spawn, theo `credentialStore.files` của invocation nếu có, không thì theo danh sách của account. **Luật chép (2026-10-19, thay luật "thiếu một file thì từ chối"):** file có mặt thì chép, file vắng thì bỏ qua, không file nào có mặt thì từ chối `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`); symlink treo hay trỏ ra ngoài home, file không thường, đường dẫn có `..` vẫn bị từ chối. Invocation không khai store thì không được chép gì dù account nào được lease (bài học `569f72d3b`), và `assessBwrap` từ chối policy không cấp `private-home` cho invocation đọc store. Account có thể khai `credentialSources` (một store cho mỗi CLI, key là `credentialStore.use` của invocation); request của Authority (`buildConfinementRequest`) chọn store theo khoá đó, và khoá không có store thì bị từ chối trước khi worker chạy (runner.md RUL80 (account trước, CLI sau: một login store cho mỗi CLI)). Không mount thư mục account thật, không bypass flag thay sandbox.
3. Trust của workspace ghi vào store trong private home (`herdr-round.mjs` `trustStorePaths`), dẫn xuất từ store account thật — store của chính account được lease (credential source mà Authority chuyển cho adapter qua `trustAccountSource`), không phải account mà env tĩnh của invocation chỉ tới (runner.md RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)); với codex, trust từng hook của `<cwd>/.codex/hooks.json` (`[hooks.state."<đường dẫn tuyệt đối>:<event>:<nhóm>:<handler>"] trusted_hash`, băm theo luật của codex, ghim bằng test) được gieo cùng lúc, chỉ vào config của private home (không bao giờ vào config thật của account; private home bị xoá sau dispatch nên không có bước gỡ) và chỉ khi gốc repo đã được người dùng tin; với claude, các MCP server do `<cwd>/.mcp.json` khai báo được duyệt riêng cho tiến trình worker bằng `--settings` (`enabledMcpjsonServers`, thêm vào args khi chuẩn bị worker invocation; không ghi file dùng chung), cũng chỉ khi gốc repo đã được tin; `fgos doctor` check `confined-pane-accounts` báo invocation confine nào đọc store mà account không có file nào của store đó (agent sẽ khởi động chưa đăng nhập), và ghi chú file vắng.

| 2 | Package version | A semantic version string tooling (e.g. packaging commands) needs to treat the package as valid | semver string | yes | `0.1.0` |
| 3 | Distribution file allowlist | The exact set of paths shipped to anyone installing the package — everything else in the source repo is excluded | `bin`, `src`, `scripts`, `core`, `domains`, `.agents`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, the end-user documentation subset (`docs/how-to`, `docs/explanation`, and `docs/enduser-docs-index.json`), plus `packages/convention/contracts/convention.rules.v1.json`, which installed doctor needs to interpret per-rule cutoffs without duplicating native rule data, and `packages/seat-binding/contracts/seat-binding.tier-ladder.v1.json`, the tier names the runner config loader accepts, read from the same file the Seat Binding crate embeds | yes | — |
| 4 | CLI entry points | The commands exposed once installed | `fgos` → runs `bin/fgos.mjs`; `fgos-runner` → runs `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` (the autonomous-loop runner, see spec Runner) | yes | — |
| 4b | Claude Code plugin skill set | `plugins/fgOS/skills/` — the Claude Code plugin's own skill bundle, distributed via the Claude Code plugin marketplace mechanism (a separate distribution channel from the npm-installed `fgos`/`fgos-runner` CLI above). Ships two layers: hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills (`cook`, `discover`, `pick`, `submit`, ...) and mirrored `fgos-*` dev-skills plus `_shared/` for plugin-only consumers. Dev-skills are authored in `core/skills/` or `domains/*/skills/`; run `npm run build:skills` in the fgOS source repo to assemble `.agents/skills/`, generate `.claude/skills/` thin wrappers and references, and mirror dev-skills/shared fragments into the plugin. Plugin mirrors stay byte-identical to `.agents/skills/`, while Claude `SKILL.md` files are thin redirects with byte-identical frontmatter (`test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs`). Assembled Markdown carries a generated-from source header. Do not hand-edit `.agents`, generated `.claude` files, or plugin mirrors; hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills remain sources. `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (doctor check, row 7 below) detects missing or stale plugin mirrors | mirrored dev-skills + shared fragments + hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills | yes (the mirrors let plugin-only consumers dispatch dev-skills without a source checkout) | — |
| 5 | Dev checkout shell helper | An opt-in file, sourced from a contributor's own shell profile, exposing the same two CLI entry points from inside a checkout of the source repository — no install, no package fetch | one file, both commands | no (contributor's own choice) | not sourced automatically anywhere |
| 5b | Global config file | `~/.fgos/config.json` — same schema as the project-local shared config file, initialized/kept current by `fgos setup` (tsk-1ri) the same way it already handles the project-local file; project always wins any key present in both (`mergeWithGlobalConfig`, `src/config/global-config.mjs`) | one file, home-dir-relative | no (optional; a missing file is not an error, resolves to `{}`) | not created by anything except `fgos setup` |
| 5c | Machine backend registry file | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` (overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_BACKEND_REGISTRY_PATH`) — machine-local backend registry declaring confinement backends (e.g. `bwrap`, container) available on the host (`confinement-backend-registry.v1`); managed by `fgos doctor --fix` (not project-over-global merge), trust store for security isolation drivers | one file, machine-local path | no (optional; bootstrap creates default bwrap backend on demand) | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` |
| 5d | Provider-capacity runtime state | `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json` — machine-local selected-account lease/quarantine state for provider-capacity rotation. Intentionally host-global only (never project-overridden) so multiple projects sharing provider accounts coordinate concurrency and rate limits safely without starvation. It is never packaged, never committed, and never repaired by `doctor`; `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` and the `provider-capacity-state` doctor check report it, while manual clear goes through `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine ...`. An account locked for a dead login is also unlocked by one real call when a dispatch would otherwise find no usable account (the lazy-probe unlock rule, now in `docs/specs/runner.md`). Its locks are holder-lock kernel locks under the machine lock root (row 5g): `provider-state` guards this file, and `provider-account/<provider>/<account>` guards one account while a renewal or unlock probe runs through it, held until that call and every process it started have exited. The same directory holds `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`: copies of a login renewed elsewhere and waiting to be applied, a scratch home while a renewal runs, and the renewal failure cooldown; it is created only when a renewal or write-back runs and holds no credential outside those copies. | one runtime directory, home-dir-relative | no (created only when a provider account lease/quarantine/write occurs) | absent/inactive |
| 5e | Confinement attestation store state | `~/.local/state/fgos/attestations/` (or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos/attestations`, overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_ATTESTATION_STORE_PATH`) — host-global security attestation records. Intentionally host-global only (outside all agent write grants) so confined agents can never tamper with their own audit trails, preserving immutable attestation integrity across projects. | one directory, machine-local path | no (created on first confined dispatch attestation) | absent/inactive |
| 5f | Workspace customization folder | `fgos/` at the project root: tracked in the project's own git, written once as a skeleton at onboarding and never edited by fgOS afterwards. Holds the customer's own agent definitions (`fgos/agents/<name>.yaml`), which win over a definition of the same name in the installed set (RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder)). Read by `--seats @name` (runner decision 0057); the `fgctl init` skeleton is not built yet | directory | no | absent — the installed set alone applies |
| 5g | Lock directories | `<lockRoot>` = `<stateRoot>/locks` (machine-scope lock files: `full-suite`, `provider-account/<provider>/<account>`, `provider-state`, `install`) and `<fgosDir>/locks` (repo-scope lock files: `gateway`, `runner`, `sessions`, `reconcile`, `main-checkout`, `worktree-admin`, `merge-slot--<encodeURIComponent(ref)>` per target ref, `state.hot` and `state.reclaim.lock`, `porting-events.hot` and `porting-events.reclaim.lock` (the state store's hot mutex: the `.hot` record is not a kernel lock file, only the `.reclaim.lock` file is), `activation`, `observe`, and `dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>` keyed by the dispatch directory's identity after realpath; the run locks live in their run: `<workflowRunDir>/locks/advance.lock`, `<runDir>/locks/recovery.lock`), both created by `fgos setup` (the machine root with mode 0700); `stateRoot` is the single resolution of `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` §11 (`FGOS_STATE_ROOT` pinned by the host, else `FGOS_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos`, `HOME/.local/state/fgos`). There is no lock config key: the wait for the processes of a dead previous holder to exit after they are terminated is fixed at 2000 ms. Lock files are never packaged, committed or repaired; `lock-kernel-semantics`, `lock-borrow-vectors` and `lock-holders` report them (row 7) | two directories | no (created by setup) | none |
| 5h | Terminal-control directory and the `terminal` config key | `<stateRoot>/terminal` (one subdirectory per driver; allocation records and their markers, a cache of what the port opened: deleting it never closes a pane because nobody closes a pane that has no record), created by `fgos setup` with mode 0700 (the `terminal-dir` fix). One config key, `terminal` (`registerConfigDefault({id: 'terminal', key: 'terminal', shape: {allocationGraceMs: 60000, retainFailedPaneMs: null, layout: {policy: 'measured-split', minCols: 80, minRows: 20, maxPanesPerTab: 8}}})`); `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md` §9 gives each number's source. Project over global over default; the merge adds a missing key only. No new environment variable (`FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` stays, as the input of `attach`). Checked 2026-10-18: the release active in the forgentX, mdview and mcp-skill-hub workspaces (one digest) accepts a `terminal` section in the global and in the project config, so the key is written like `lock`; had it refused unknown keys, setup would have written it to the project config only until all three workspaces ran the new release. | `<stateRoot>/terminal` present / absent; config key present / absent | yes (computed, not stored) | — |
| 6 | Config staleness | Whether a config file (project-local or global — same computation, tsk-1ri) already has every setting the current default schema defines | up to date / missing one or more default settings | yes (computed, not stored) | — |
| 7 | Doctor check | One named diagnostic `fgos doctor` reports on | not a fixed list — an extensible registry (`src/setup/registrations.mjs`'s `registerCheck`); a check registration and a config-default registration are independent, never a forced pairing — a module may register only a check, only a config-default, or both. Today's registered checks: `convention-conformance`, `identity-project-id` (this repository carries one project id in the tracked file `.fgos/project.json`, asked through `fgos identity project --json`; absent only warns and there is no fix, because a fix on every machine would mint one id per clone: `fgos identity project --init` runs once on one machine, the file is committed and the others pull it; an unreadable or invalid file fails), `node-version-and-git`, `cli-version-visible` (tsk-2ej), `shell-integration-sourced`, `project-fgos-launcher` (a release install has one fgos launcher on PATH that runs each project's own activated fgos, see RUL17 (one fgos on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos)), `config-not-stale`, `main-checkout-hook-wired`, `tool-registry-configured`, `work-classification-vocabulary`, `work-step-vocabulary` (tsk-64h), `domain-workflow-operations-coverage`, `root-drift`, `delivered-not-on-trunk` (tsk-1l9), `config-awareness`, `provider-capacity-state` (reports account lease/quarantine state and never auto-clears), `credential-copies-retained` (login copies still pending for a renewal after a day, and private homes held after repeated staging failures, counted by provider/account and age; read-only, a held home fails, copies waiting for a renewal only warn, and, when the machine-global provider inventory was read, copies of any age in a store directory the account's login store layout no longer reads fail, naming the directory for hand recovery (when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator the check fails, says the layout was not checked with the reason, lists copies at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch); interrupted stagings (pending/.tmp-*) are reported too once their writer is gone and they have sat for ten minutes, and the over-limit line names the store; kept homes under a registered backend's temp and private-home roots are scanned, which the orphan reaper check does not do, and one there counts as held at once because nothing retries it; the check itself never deletes and never prints a value), `lock-kernel-semantics` (for the workspace lock directory and the machine lock root: the holder-lock driver's guarantee through the in-process door, then a two-process probe on that same mount, a description locked here and handed to a child must read held while the child lives and free once it died; prints driver, exclusion, borrow and holders levels, then the state root with its source and the fixed 2000 ms kill wait; kernel with a green probe passes, a missing directory warns until setup creates it, a guarantee of unsupported (a platform with no driver), a network filesystem none, an unresolved state root and an unreachable door fail by name; on Windows the probe runs over a lock-hold helper and the message shows lockfileex), `lock-borrow-vectors` (runs the host's lock-borrow-vectors route: a lock description borrowed by a git child must not leak to any background process git starts; any red vector or a red sibling check fails, unavailable fails, since activation refuses the same result and there is no run-time switch that disables borrowing; runs on Windows with its own pid-handle assertion), `lock-holders` (for every existing lock file of the locks this release cut over, including the main checkout, merge slot and worktree-admin files, the holders the kernel lists: a holder whose origin is foreign (neither a fgOS process, by the host's state-root pin or a fgOS payload in its argv, nor a borrowed child of that lock) warns with pid and cmdline; a predecessor record next to a lock file naming a domain that is not empty, an unknown record version or a Windows job the host does not judge empty warns with the domain and the reason; the state and porting-events hot records of the workspace, under .fgos/locks, warn with the path and the fence command of the lock verb when a record does not parse or its holder cannot be placed for more than five minutes (absent, alive or dead holders pass; no automatic fix, because a person confirms the holder is gone); holders that cannot be listed are informational), `dependencies-installed`, `gate-bypass-configured`, `claude-plugin-marketplace`, `plugin-skill-cli-reachable`, `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (tsk-32b), `changelog-unreleased-stale`, `herdr-launcher-configured`, `herdr-web-dashboard-configured` (tsk-48w), `enduser-docs-index-stale` (tsk-1m0), `invariant-checks-configured` (tsk-516), `invocation-git-write-grants` (warns when an invocation or executor still grants a git add or git commit tool; the runner commits, workers only edit files; read-only, never rewrites user config), `worktree-setup-configured` (a present worktreeSetup section is a list of non-empty shell commands every runner-created worktree runs after its dependency install; never executes them), `events-jsonl-not-truncated` (tsk-cgg), `worker-slots-ceiling-usable` (tsk-1oz), `gateway-token-configured` (tsk-4r1), `readme-install-tag-exists` (tsk-2t8), `iron-law-configured` (tsk-1y6-1), `leaf-notify-drift` (tsk-1el), `task-specs-resolve` (tsk-2t9c), `agent-claims-resolve` (tsk-2t9c), `agent-type-names-unique` (tsk-397-12; names unique within each tier fgos/agents, domains/*/agents, core/agents, a higher tier replaces a lower one whole, the fgos/agents files checked for shape), `domain-registry-compiled` (every domain's compiled.json file under domains — the precompiled form of the registry and workflow YAML the Work lifecycle reads, regenerated by the build:domains npm script; the check reports a missing, unreadable or stale file and domain YAML that cannot be parsed, and a drift test keeps it equal to the YAML), `dispatch-decide-hook-wired` (tsk-60f; also requires the AskUserQuestion decision-question hook), `codex-hook-wired`, `agy-hook-wired`, `omp-hook-wired`, `pi-hook-wired`, `decision-index-stale` (tsk-1lv-2/tsk-1lv), `advise-execute-capabilities-configured` (tsk-2uf-3), `workflow-capabilities-configured` (every capability a core/domain Workflow unit names resolves in runner.capabilities by exact name or bare verb, the way bind() looks it up, and fails when it does not; one that resolves but has no "prefer" pool on either name is reported as a warning because bind() refuses its unit headless; fgos setup registers every shipped Workflow's capabilities as description-only defaults, so a fresh project starts with that warning, and never overwrites a project's own entry), `capability-serves-valid` (I19: every runner.capabilities entry's serves attribute set is well-formed, no two entries declare the identical set, and the review slot is present), `agy-permissions-configured` (tsk-1xm), `agy-sub-homes-configured`, `bwrap-available`, `curl-available` (curl runs, because fgctl init downloads a release through it; a missing curl is a warning that only blocks the download paths, never a failure, see RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given)), `main-checkout-guard-warnings` (tsk-1vc-3), `events-compaction-verified` (tsk-3ve-6), `no-stuck-merge-abort` (tsk-40a), `doc-registry-enforce` (tsk-28x), `doc-registry-stale` (tsk-28x), `doc-alias-broken` (tsk-28x), `doc-active-duplicate` (tsk-28x), `doc-near-duplicate` (tsk-28x), `doc-provisional-aged` (tsk-28x), `doc-topic-oversized` (tsk-28x), `doc-role-underused` (tsk-28x), `doc-source-conservation` (tsk-28x), `doc-current-path-missing` (tsk-3uc), `doc-source-unreachable` (tsk-3uc), `coordination-protocol-fixtures-valid` (retired; confirms legacy definition fixtures retired), `operation-prompt-templates-valid` (Phase 03 I04: every discoverable operation prompt template validates against bounded variables and schema), `coordination-example-requests-valid` (Step 08 Phase 07 R3: published fgos coordination run example request files validate against the same schema boundary the CLI itself enforces, and resolve every referenced protocolRef), `terminal-control` (the terminal-control driver answers through the internal route: driver, declared capabilities and the herdr server incarnation are printed; a missing herdr only warns, a missing layout.geometry capability is information, and a bad FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE fails), `terminal-config` (the terminal section after the merge, each value with its source; fails by name on a grace below the ready timeout plus 30 s, a retain time that is neither null nor a positive integer, an unregistered policy, or limits that are not positive integers or sit below the measured floor of 40x8), `terminal-allocations` (slots past terminal.allocationGraceMs that never launched and retained panes past their time, from the route's reconcile-scan; reports only, closes nothing), `trust-store-readable`, `non-claude-trust-stores-readable` (Phase 07 herdr-trust-supervisor R3: every executor or invocation declaring a codex-toml or agy/agy-json trustStore reads from a store that is actually readable, using the same reader the live dispatch will use), `confined-pane-accounts` (every confined herdr invocation that binds a private home has an account in the machine-global provider account inventory whose credential files exist, so its pane starts logged in; see RUL65b in the runner spec), `agent-cli-project-trusted` (the project root is trusted in every codex home and agy sub-HOME the configured executors run under, so a headless dispatch does not stop at a "Trust this folder?" prompt until its timeout; reads only a yes/no for the one path, names the exact line a person must add, never edits the CLI's config; not applicable when the root is not a git repository or no codex/agy executor is configured), `seat-binding-dry-bind` (binds every seat of every Workflow unit through the runner's own pattern code, in a fixed headless session with no lease, and fails on a policy refusal such as a missing tier cell or an independence rule the pool cannot meet; no pool, account state, tier caps and shared families are information), `blind-steps-use-proven-pools` (for every Workflow unit declared blind, walks each role's candidates through bind() without dispatching anything and fails when the capability prefer pool can bind an executor whose provider family, transport and confinement backend are not in the table of canary-proven pairs kept in the check's own module; read-only, no model call; not applicable when no unit is blind), `executor-posture-coverage` (core capabilities execute, code:implement, and capabilities declaring a pool have at least one candidate executor capable of applying required posture; dry simulation via bind(), no process spawn), `executor-confinement` (dispatch visibility V0 Phase 01 group D: the transport an interactive dispatch needs, a readable folder-trust store so a fresh worktree can be pre-trusted instead of stopping at a dialog, and a second reading of the rule that an executor may only declare bypass permission mode alongside full confinement), `herdr-executor-kinds` (Phase 05 R3: every executor dispatched through a herdr pane names an agent kind herdr can actually start, and none depends on an integration hook herdr reports as outdated -- an installed-but-stale hook is believed by herdr and may report the wrong agent state, while a missing one only degrades detection), `executor-profile-warnings` (Phase 06 executor-policy-dispatch-seams: legacy executor/capability entries hardcoding policy-shaped flags, policy-overrides-as-identity, or account-pool-shaped env, each named with its documented migration target -- informational only, never a hard failure), `active-release-matches-checkout` (read-only Node payload contents against doctor dir working tree, not HEAD or Rust binary freshness; reports changed/missing/extra source files while excluding staged dependencies, skips outside source checkouts and main-owned activation in linked worktrees; use fgos:dev for working-tree code or restage/activate for plain fgos), `rust-host-binary-present`, `rust-host-target-supported`, `legacy-node-payload-present`, `command-routes-drift`, `confinement-policies-declared`, `confinement-backend-registry-readable`, `confinement-bwrap-platform`, `confinement-probe-freshness`, `confinement-blind-read` (a blind unit can be enforced: the registered bwrap backend hides peer run state, homes and processes from a worker; reports pass, fail, or backend-unsupported, in which case every blind unit is refused), `confinement-strict-readiness`, `confinement-orphaned-resources-reaped` (Phase 04 M8: no confinement temp resource is left behind by a dead owning process, and no confinement temp root is readable beyond its owner; a home kept for a still-open pane is not orphaned; the fix tightens the root to 0700 and reaps), `confinement-herdr-maturity`, `instruction-projections-stale`, `runner-coordination-orgPolicy-shape`, `operation-capability-resolves` (Unit I21: every discoverable operation's declared policy.capability resolves against the live runner config, reporting reachable provider-family diversity), `shadow-binder-divergence` (dispatch-engine-liveness-hardening Phase 7 C1: real PlacementPolicy/ProviderAdapter shadow-binder divergence is durably recorded to a local JSONL under .fgos/dispatch/, not only an ephemeral stderr line; informational, never fails), `observe-dir-writable`, `observe-friction-migrated`, `observe-host-resolvable`, `writer-identity-resolvable` (the writer identity resolves through the Rust host for both the running host and the workspace activation a plain git commit hook uses; each binary is asked directly, so an older activated release shows as a version mismatch), `identity-machine-id` (this machine has an id minted by the Identity component, asked through `fgos identity machine --json`; absent only warns, `fgos doctor --fix` mints it once and never replaces it; an unreadable or invalid file fails), `observe-run-coverage`, `coordination-protocol-dead-vocabulary` (validates definitions against dead vocabulary), `model-policy-tier-coverage` (validates model policies cover the default tier, runner.defaults.tier, for every registered executor), `executor-family-unique` (two agent executors of one provider family fail, naming both), `executor-skills-installed` (every skill an agent executor declares in its supports.skills has a SKILL.md in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout, chosen by each invocation's CLI (claude: .claude/skills, codex: .agents/skills, omp: .omp/skills, pi: .pi/skills, grok: .grok/skills), every invocation of an executor must have the skill; a missing one fails naming the path and the remedy; a CLI with no known skill directory is reported as not checked), `model-policy-pools` (a tier cell entry model@pool whose pool runner.llmAccounts does not declare warns; not evaluated when no cell names a pool), `llm-accounts-shape` (every problem the runner.llmAccounts reader finds fails: an inventory in the project config, a pool name with an at-sign or another spelling of a family, an account without a credentialStore directory), `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` (when runner.llmAccounts is declared, accounts or login directories that differ from runner.providers, which the lease still reads, warn), `global-model-policies-portable` (a list or model@pool cell in the global runner.modelPolicies fails, since older releases on the machine cannot read it), `tier-fallback` (a family `runner.tierFallback` lists for a tier that has no `modelPolicies` cell at that tier, or no agent executor, warns: the walk skips it; never fails), `tier-vocabulary-dead-keys` (validates project and global config do not contain retired tier/rigor keys), `runner-patterns-config` (validates presence, valid checkers, and cumulative checkersByRigor for runner patterns), `runner-generated-paths` (validates runner.generatedPaths source-to-render-target mappings), `process-containment`, `run-supervisor-route`, `runtime-socket-dir`, `run-attempts-stuck`, `gate-kill-grace`, `legacy-attempts-stuck`, `units-awaiting-resume`, `cancel-wait`. The registry is open, but this list is not a snapshot — it names every registered check, and a module adding one updates this row in the same change | yes | — |
| 7b | Doctor fix | One named repair `fgos doctor --fix` can run before re-reporting checks | not a fixed list — an extensible registry (`registerFix`), independent of `registerCheck`/`registerConfigDefault` (per tsk-2cs). Today's registered fixes: `credential-copies-retained` (re-checks private homes held after repeated staging failures, and any kept home under a registered backend's own root, which nothing else retries, under the account lock, and removes one only when its login is shown applied or obsolete; also removes an interrupted staging (pending/.tmp-*) only after claiming it by rename, when its writer is gone and it is empty, identical to a copy already kept, or shown no newer than the source login under the account lock; never removes on age), `gate-bypass-configured` (tsk-2qz, the registry's first entry to register all three capabilities at once), `claude-plugin-marketplace` (tsk-4xg), `enduser-docs-index-stale` (tsk-1m0), `bin-discovery-cache` (tsk-2qc-1), `gateway-token-configured` (tsk-4r1), `iron-law-configured` (tsk-1y6-1), `decision-index-stale` (tsk-1lv-2/tsk-1lv), `agy-permissions-configured` (tsk-1xm), `no-stuck-merge-abort` (tsk-40a), `doc-registry-stale` (tsk-28x), `confinement-backend-registry-readable`, `confinement-orphaned-resources-reaped` (Phase 04 M8), `terminal-dir` (creates the terminal directory under the state root with mode 0700 when missing, and tightens an existing one to 0700), `lock-dirs` (creates the workspace lock directory and the machine lock root with mode 0700 when missing, and tightens an existing one to 0700, since the first lock taken before setup may have created it with the umask's mode), `instruction-projections-stale`, `runner-coordination-orgPolicy-shape`, `project-fgos-launcher`, `dispatch-decide-hook-wired`, `codex-hook-wired`, `agy-hook-wired`, `omp-hook-wired`, `pi-hook-wired`, `runtime-socket-dir`, `run-attempts-stuck`, `legacy-attempts-stuck`. Same rule as #7: the registry is open, but this list names every registered fix and a module adding one updates this row in the same change | yes | — |
| 7c | Doctor check `process-containment` | Which process-containment driver this machine would pick for an attempt (`bwrap-pidns`, `linux-pgroup`, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), the level it gives and the named escapes; read from the host route's `--protocol 1 --probe` answer (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` §14, `docs/platform/process/spec.md` §10) | passed with `kernel`; warning with the name `best-effort` (Linux without a user namespace, macOS); never a failure for being best-effort | yes (computed) | — |
| 7d | Doctor check `runtime-socket-dir` | The run supervisor's runtime socket directory (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/fgos`, else `/tmp/fgos-<uid>`): exists, mode 0700, owned by the user, short enough for a unix socket path. `fgos setup` creates it; the fix creates it too | passed / failed (missing, wrong owner or mode, too long) | yes (computed) | created by setup |
| 7e | Doctor check `run-attempts-stuck` | Runs with an envelope v3 and no `closed.json` whose attempt lock is free, counted by `fgos internal adopt --scan --probe-only` (writes nothing, takes no lock); the fix drives them to closed through the one sweep (`sweepAttempts`) | passed / warning with the count | yes (computed) | — |
| 7f | Doctor check `run-supervisor-route` | The active host binary answers `--protocol 1 --probe` with `result: ok` for each of `fgos internal supervise`, `gate`, `adopt`, `attempt-step` | passed / failed naming the route or the protocol mismatch | yes (computed) | — |
| 7g | Doctor check `gate-kill-grace` | The config key `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` (the SIGTERM to SIGKILL grace of the launch gate): value and source (`project`, `global`, `default`); project overrides global; setup does not write the key into the global config until every workspace runs a release that knows it | passed with the value (absent: default 10000); failed when not an integer or below 1000 | yes (computed) | 10000 |
| 7h | Doctor check `cancel-wait` | The config key `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (how long a controller stopped by Ctrl-C or SIGTERM waits for its attempts' receipts), read by the same reader as `gate-kill-grace`: value and source (`project`, `global`, `default` = grace + 5000); an unusable value, below 1000 or shorter than the grace, fails | yes (computed) | — |
| 7i | Doctor check `legacy-attempts-stuck` | Runs from before the run supervisor still `running`: fails while one is provably dead (every recorded pid dead, no version-1 home), warns with the reason for each run that is kept; fix settles the provable ones as `abandoned-legacy` | yes (computed) | settled in `run.json` by fix |
| 7j | Doctor check `units-awaiting-resume` | Unit runs whose controller is gone and whose last attempt is closed, with the `fgos run --resume <unit>` command; warns, never fails | yes (computed) | — |
| 8 | Output rendering mode | How `fgos setup`/`fgos doctor` present their result | enveloped JSON (every other verb's shape, unchanged) / colored plain text (`--pretty`) | yes | enveloped JSON |

## Data Dictionary

| # | Element | Meaning | Values | Required | Default |
|---|-------|---------|--------|----------|---------|

previous.text: #### 5. ReleaseManifest
previous.sectionText:
#### 5. ReleaseManifest

The release manifest is the immutable statement of what an fgOS release
contains.

The canonical artifact digest is computed from this release tree manifest, not
from a `.zip`, `.tar.gz`, npm package archive, or transport wrapper. Archive
digests may still be recorded for download/integrity diagnostics, but they are
not runtime identity. Runtime identity must survive different compression
formats, package transports, and mirror locations.

The digest formula is:

```txt
fileDigest = sha256(file bytes as emitted by the release build)
artifactDigest = sha256(canonical-json(release tree manifest without artifactDigest))
```

The release build, not the installer, owns byte normalization. Install should
not rewrite line endings or file contents to make a digest pass.

Minimum fields:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "artifactDigest": "sha256:...",
  "digestKind": "release-tree-manifest",
  "releaseVersion": "0.1.0",
  "sourceRevision": "...",
  "createdAt": "2026-09-04T00:00:00Z",
  "target": {
    "os": "linux",
    "arch": "x64",
    "libc": "glibc"
  },
  "entries": {
    "fgos": "bin/fgos",
    "fgosRunner": "bin/fgos-runner"
  },
  "components": {
    "legacyNode": {
      "root": "libexec/legacy-node",
      "entry": "bin/fgos.mjs",
      "digest": "sha256:..."
    },
    "runner": {
      "path": "bin/fgos-runner",
      "digest": "sha256:..."
    },
    "workshop": {
      "skillsDigest": "sha256:...",
      "agentsDigest": "sha256:...",
      "proseDigest": "sha256:..."
    }
  },
  "requires": {
    "node": ">=20 <23",
    "git": ">=2.39"
  },
  "adapter": {
    "protocolVersion": "1",
    "entry": "bin/fgos adapter",
    "capabilities": []
  },
  "stateSchemas": {
    "read": ["1"],
    "write": ["1"],
    "migrations": []
  },
  "files": []
}
```

`components.legacyNode` names a payload **root** plus an **entry** inside it, not a single file (proposed 2026-09-10 by the host-invocation stream, see [Legacy CLI Transition](../../../architect/host-invocation-routing/legacy-cli-transition.md) §2): the legacy payload is the whole Node package as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged with its source-relative layout intact so `bin/fgos.mjs` needs no import changes, and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` lives in the same root. The Rust host resolves `join(activeReleasePath, root, entry)` and nothing else. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: "."`, `entry: "bin/fgos.mjs"`, `entries.fgos: "target/release/fgos"` — the same fields serve dogfood and a staged release.

next.text: ##### Release Tree Canonicalization
next.sectionText:
##### Release Tree Canonicalization

V1 uses a logical release file tree, not raw filesystem metadata.

| Field / Rule | V1 Decision |
|---|---|
| Path root | All paths are relative to the release root. Absolute paths are invalid. |
| Path separator | Always `/`, including on Windows. |
| Path normalization | UTF-8 NFC normalization before ordering and digesting. |
| Path order | Lexicographic byte order after normalization. |
| Case collision | Refuse a release if two paths collide under case-insensitive comparison. |
| File digest | SHA-256 of exact release-build bytes. |
| Line endings | Included in file bytes. Build must normalize if needed; install must not rewrite. |
| Executable bit | Included as `mode`, at least `755` vs `644`. |
| Directory entries | Not hashed as separate entries; directories are inferred from file paths. |
| Symlink | Refused in V1. Add explicit `kind: "symlink"` later only with relative, non-escaping targets. |
| mtime / owner / group | Excluded from runtime identity. |
| Archive digest | Optional `transportDigest`; never the runtime identity. |

Each file entry should include an ownership class:

```json
{
  "path": "bin/fgos",
  "kind": "file",
  "digest": "sha256:...",
  "mode": "755",
  "class": "immutable-entry"
}
```

Initial classes:

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `immutable-entry` | Public executable entry included in the release. |
| `immutable-runtime` | Runtime implementation/provider file. |
| `immutable-workshop-source` | Canonical skills, agents, or prose shipped with the runtime. |
| `immutable-doc` | Shipped documentation/prose used by users or agents. |
| `metadata` | Manifest or metadata file that participates in release identity. |

Generated workspace projections are not recorded as release-tree files at
their projected workspace paths. The release manifest records their canonical
source material; `ProjectionLedger` records where that material was projected
inside the workspace.

`files` may eventually contain every immutable release file and digest. The
minimum useful fingerprint set is:

- public entry binaries;
- provider descriptors;
- active host entry at `bin/fgos` whether implemented by Node first or Rust
  later;
- legacy Node payload;
- runner;
- adapter metadata/entry;
- init/doctor registries;
- skills, agents, prose source;
- manifest files themselves.

previous.text:
| Field / Rule | V1 Decision |
|---|---|
| Path root | All paths are relative to the release root. Absolute paths are invalid. |
| Path separator | Always `/`, including on Windows. |
| Path normalization | UTF-8 NFC normalization before ordering and digesting. |
| Path order | Lexicographic byte order after normalization. |
| Case collision | Refuse a release if two paths collide under case-insensitive comparison. |
| File digest | SHA-256 of exact release-build bytes. |
| Line endings | Included in file bytes. Build must normalize if needed; install must not rewrite. |
| Executable bit | Included as `mode`, at least `755` vs `644`. |
| Directory entries | Not hashed as separate entries; directories are inferred from file paths. |
| Symlink | Refused in V1. Add explicit `kind: "symlink"` later only with relative, non-escaping targets. |
| mtime / owner / group | Excluded from runtime identity. |
| Archive digest | Optional `transportDigest`; never the runtime identity. |

next.text: ## Canonical Release Tree Rules
next.sectionText:
## Canonical Release Tree Rules

This section owns the complete selected V1 manifest rules used by `canonical.rs` and `verify.rs`, conserved verbatim below (including NFC, byte ordering, collisions, exclusions and digest calculation). Existing checked amendments elsewhere in this contract still qualify implementation status; no preflight or schema correction is undone.


The release manifest is the immutable statement of what an fgOS release
contains.

The canonical artifact digest is computed from this release tree manifest, not
from a `.zip`, `.tar.gz`, npm package archive, or transport wrapper. Archive
digests may still be recorded for download/integrity diagnostics, but they are
not runtime identity. Runtime identity must survive different compression
formats, package transports, and mirror locations.

The digest formula is:

```txt
fileDigest = sha256(file bytes as emitted by the release build)
artifactDigest = sha256(canonical-json(release tree manifest without artifactDigest))
```

The release build, not the installer, owns byte normalization. Install should
not rewrite line endings or file contents to make a digest pass.

Minimum fields:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "artifactDigest": "sha256:...",
  "digestKind": "release-tree-manifest",
  "releaseVersion": "0.1.0",
  "sourceRevision": "...",
  "createdAt": "2026-09-04T00:00:00Z",
  "target": {
    "os": "linux",
    "arch": "x64",
    "libc": "glibc"
  },
  "entries": {
    "fgos": "bin/fgos",
    "fgosRunner": "bin/fgos-runner"
  },
  "components": {
    "legacyNode": {
      "root": "libexec/legacy-node",
      "entry": "bin/fgos.mjs",
      "digest": "sha256:..."
    },
    "runner": {
      "path": "bin/fgos-runner",
      "digest": "sha256:..."
    },
    "workshop": {
      "skillsDigest": "sha256:...",
      "agentsDigest": "sha256:...",
      "proseDigest": "sha256:..."
    }
  },
  "requires": {
    "node": ">=20 <23",
    "git": ">=2.39"
  },
  "adapter": {
    "protocolVersion": "1",
    "entry": "bin/fgos adapter",
    "capabilities": []
  },
  "stateSchemas": {
    "read": ["1"],
    "write": ["1"],
    "migrations": []
  },
  "files": []
}
```

`components.legacyNode` names a payload **root** plus an **entry** inside it, not a single file (proposed 2026-09-10 by the host-invocation stream, see [Legacy CLI Transition](../host-invocation-routing/legacy-cli-transition.md) §2): the legacy payload is the whole Node package as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged with its source-relative layout intact so `bin/fgos.mjs` needs no import changes, and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` lives in the same root. The Rust host resolves `join(activeReleasePath, root, entry)` and nothing else. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: "."`, `entry: "bin/fgos.mjs"`, `entries.fgos: "target/release/fgos"` — the same fields serve dogfood and a staged release.
