selected.text:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`; `no-confined-cli` when no probed invocation declares a sandbox). The verdict reads only the rows whose invocation declares its own sandbox (`confined: true`, each row's `inVerdict`): the read-only posture makes the door confine every round (`resolvePosture` returns a required `host-write-denied` requirement), and an invocation that declares no sandbox binds no private home either, so its CLI meets its own login directory (`CODEX_HOME`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) mounted read-only and stops on `EROFS` before it answers. That row is still run and reported (outcome `sandbox`, truthfully: a read-only dispatch pinned to that invocation fails the same way), but it says nothing about the account or the CLI (2026-10-13: tetcu72, fgovn and tetnu answered on every sandboxed invocation while `pi-cli-` and `codex-cli-bypass-fgovn` died on `EROFS` under `local-bwrap-v1`, and the verdict read `cli-fault`). The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(, )`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(, )`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose. - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **RUL104 (`fgos run --resume` after a controller death takes the settled attempt through adopt and never runs the agent twice; Ctrl-C cancels; 2026-10-18; owner decision 2026-10-16).** A unit whose controller died never continues on its own: it reads `unitState: awaiting-resume` (last attempt `closed`, no `unit-summary.json`, no live controller; shown by `dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json`) and only an explicit `--resume` goes on. Resume asks adopt about the last attempt of every seat and round before anything else: `closed` with a result is the attempt's result and the unit carries on from it (commit `writes`, reviewer, next attempt, `unit-summary.json`), so the agent runs once; a `cancelled`, `abandoned-not-started` or `abandoned-before-brief` receipt is superseded, a new attempt runs the unit again and names the old one in `supersedesRunId` (set only on a new launch; the old attempt reads `superseded`); a `gate-lost` receipt (binding present, gate dead, no `gate-exit`) is not relaunched, a named limit: adopt cannot prove the agent never ran, so it fails closed (r6 §9.7) rather than risk running it twice, and the person starts a new `fgos run`; `running` and `being-adopted` are refused `attempt-still-running` (resume does not wait); `legacy-run` is refused `attempt-legacy-run` (doctor `legacy-attempts-stuck` settles it as `abandoned-legacy`, which is closed for the unit); a second concurrent `--resume` of the unit finds the controller seat (`unit-control` ledger) held by a live controller and is refused `resume-in-progress`. Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.

previous.text: - **RUL76 (`execute <executorId> --for <capability>`: the caller states the posture; [ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL77 (posture thuộc capability; agent executor không khai `for`) — chốt "executor phải khai capability" đã bỏ]; partly reverses the `execute --for` retirement of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch; `execute --for` đã rút), 2026-10-13).** `execute <id>` with no purpose infers the capability from the executor's own `for` list, a required-confinement capability first (`resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints`). RUL70 (executor id theo `providerModel`; gộp `pi`+`codex` thành `openai`) merged `codex` (`for: [code:review, code:debug]`, both `host-write-denied`) and `pi` (no `for`, the writing invocations) into `openai`, so every `execute openai` became write-denied, whatever the work: a documentation task died with `Read-only file system` when Codex tried to refresh its login under bwrap. That rule itself says executors whose `for` differ should not be merged into one entry; the merge kept the codex `for` without noticing pi had none. Instead of splitting the executor, the two-phase `decide`-then-`execute` pattern now carries the purpose to phase two: `execute <id> --for <capability>` runs under that capability's posture. It is accepted only when the executor declares the capability in `for` or the capability's `prefer` names the executor (otherwise `capability-not-served`, before spawning), so config still says which postures an executor accepts; without `--for` the strictest-first inference stays the fail-closed default. `execute --for` with no executor, or combined with `--assignment`/`--contract`, is still refused. `openai.for` gains `execute`, so writing work goes `execute openai --for execute`, which takes the first `cli` invocation (`codex-cli-bypass-fgovn`, unconfined). `--timeout-ms`/`--idle-timeout-ms` override `runner.timeoutMs`/`runner.idleTimeoutMs` per call. Config for a dispatch whose `--cwd` is a worktree with its own `.fgos/config.json` is read from that worktree (5a42bc376, intended), so a branch behind main also resolves older model tiers.

## Edge Cases Settled

- Worker `cli-spawn` chạy trong sandbox (bwrap) chỉ ghi được dưới `runs/<n>/worker-output/outbox`: effective contract và prompt gọi tên claim/report ở đó (không phải thư mục run phẳng, vốn read-only → `EROFS`); collector, reconcile run chết và lần chọn thao tác sau đều tìm claim/report qua cùng một lookup (`worker-output/outbox`, rồi `worker-output`, rồi `outbox`, rồi tên phẳng). herdr-spawn giữ outbox riêng của brief.
- Runner bị giết giữa việc: lần chạy sau gặt lại đúng trạng thái (proof đạt → awaiting-approval, không → blocked), nhánh có ĐÚNG MỘT commit worker — test giết thật.
- Nhánh bị worktree mồ côi giữ (path còn hoặc đã mất) đều đòi lại được — bug thật do e2e bắt sau khi code ship, vá bằng cell fix-first (phase-2-routing-10).
- Đề xuất bị người duyệt trả (`awaiting-approval→todo` kèm lý do): việc vào lại frontier, chống-lặp đếm và chặn lặp vô hạn.
- Kho chưa init / frontier trống: vòng kết thúc sạch, không nghi thức.
- Hai lần chạy chồng lấp: lần hai thoát «bận» — 0 ghi trạng thái, 0 thao tác worktree, khoá của lần một còn nguyên vẹn. Khoá mồ côi (chủ đã chết, hoặc nội dung rác) → lượt gặp nó dọn đi rồi vẫn lui ra «bận»; lượt kế tiếp chiếm khoá sạch và chạy bình thường (sau crash: hai lượt là phục hồi xong).
- Cách ly vị trí của worker có by construction: worktree nằm trong thư mục tạm hệ thống — đường walk-up từ cwd của worker không bao giờ gặp xưởng/harness phát triển.
- `fgos-runner` khởi động trên một repo git 0 commit: dừng ngay ở `validation`, nêu rõ nguyên nhân (HEAD không resolve) + cách sửa (`git commit` trước) — không claim item nào, không chạm bảng phục hồi/retry per-item, cùng phạm trù lỗi với nhánh không-phải-repo-git đã có.
- `fgos-runner` khởi động trên một repo git có ≥1 commit: hành vi không đổi một byte so với trước quyết định này — `resolveRepoRoot` vẫn trả về đúng chuỗi repo root như cũ.
- Việc bị đỗ-lại hoặc bị dừng cũng để lại bản ghi thực tế (outcome) — vòng học nhìn thấy thất bại, không chỉ thành công; đọc lại được qua `fgos metrics outcomes` — chứng minh bằng một lần dispatch thật (không chỉ fixture).
- Quét nghiên-cứu gặp worker sập giữa chừng, hoặc chạy xong mà không để lại commit nào: không crash vòng chạy — item nằm nguyên `discovery`/`todo` cho lượt quét sau thử lại, không bao giờ bị đẩy tiếp âm thầm; lượt chạy vẫn tiếp tục xử các item khác — chứng minh bằng e2e fail-safe qua binary thật.
- Item vừa được quét nghiên-cứu đẩy sang `planning` trong CÙNG lượt chạy: quét chia-việc ngay bên dưới đọc view tươi nên nhặt được nó trong chính lượt đó, không đợi lượt kế tiếp. Nó chỉ đi tiếp tới dispatch trong cùng lượt khi bản kế hoạch của chính nó đã khai là việc một-mảnh; còn lại nó dừng ở `planning` chờ một phiên sống phán tay — chứng minh bằng e2e một lượt `--once` đưa item từ `discovery` tới `planning` với status vẫn `todo` (không bị claim, không bị đề xuất).
- Ngã-ngũ tự động của runner trong một lượt dispatch thật (quét nghiên-cứu, nhận việc, đề xuất, đỗ) đều mang đúng `role` = `runner`; ngã-ngũ đóng tay qua CLI mang `role` = `human` — chứng minh bằng benchmark F4 chạy qua binary thật (không chỉ fixture), round 2: 6/6 tiêu chí đạt.
- `check` chạy hai lần liên tiếp trên cùng kho: lần hai luôn in phần chênh lệch entropy thật so lần một, kể cả khi điểm không đổi (in "+0 so lần trước", không im lặng) — chứng minh bằng benchmark thật.
- Một kênh seal-digest có số đếm khác 0 nhưng chênh lệch bằng 0 (không có gì mới kể từ lần trước) vẫn in ra — chỉ kênh trống tuyệt đối (số đếm 0 VÀ chênh lệch 0) mới im lặng hoàn toàn (bài học rút ra từ một lần khai sai kỳ vọng ở benchmark F4 vòng 1, sửa lại đúng ở vòng 2).
- Item đơn giản đi qua quét nghiên-cứu rồi quét chia-việc trong CÙNG một lượt chạy `--once`: chuỗi `discovery → planning → executing` hoàn tất và item tới `awaiting-approval` trước khi lượt chạy đó kết thúc — với điều kiện bản kế hoạch của nó khai một-mảnh; nếu không, nó dừng ở `planning` chờ người, và đó cũng là kết cục ĐÚNG — chứng minh bằng e2e một lượt duy nhất qua binary thật.
- Một phiên đi qua lớp hướng dẫn giai đoạn (P50) hỏi một item rõ ràng: skill làm-rõ sàng lọc câu hỏi ứng viên không đạt (chỉ ảnh hưởng người-triển-khai) và không tạo cổng chờ-người — item đi thẳng, không hỏi oan (chứng minh bằng case-study 2026-07-20).
- Engine tự phán "chưa đủ rõ" NGAY CẢ với một item khách quan rõ ràng, khi lời gọi phán-đoán bên dưới thất bại vì lý do hạ tầng (không phải vì item mơ hồ) — cổng chờ-người thật vẫn nổi lên đúng theo thiết kế fail-safe (không bao giờ coi phán đoán không chắc là pass); lớp hướng dẫn không tự trả lời thay, escalate đúng luật (chứng minh bằng case-study 2026-07-20, xem Open Gaps).
- Item phức tạp sinh ≥2 con qua một phán quyết chia-việc: gốc bị bộ lọc frontier chặn (lineage qua `parent`, không qua `deps`) cho tới khi cả hai con tới `done`; con cuối đóng xong, gốc tự lọt frontier ở lượt kế tiếp và runner tự chạy verify CỦA CHÍNH GỐC (mang từ lúc rời vòng làm-rõ) làm goal-check — chứng minh bằng e2e qua binary thật, không chỉ fixture.
- Item mơ hồ ở chia-việc (verdict cần người quyết, hoặc gốc mang risk `heavy`): đậu `awaiting-human` mang đề xuất chia làm câu hỏi; người trả lời xong, lượt phán sau phán lại từ đầu (không giữ đề xuất cũ) — chứng minh bằng e2e round-trip qua binary thật, cùng khuôn parity với vòng nghiên-cứu.
- Quét chia-việc không bao giờ tự gọi model, nên không có đường "model trả rác" ở bước này; còn một phán quyết chia tay mà có con thiếu verify thì bị từ chối — gốc ở nguyên trạng thái/stage hiện tại, không con nào được ghi, lượt chạy vẫn tiếp tục xử các item khác.
- Gặt-lại lúc khởi động SKIP một item `doing` mang `claimRole` người/phiên (cửa pull), dù item đó không mang commit/proof nào — nhưng vẫn gặt bình thường một claim mồ côi của chính runner ở cùng lượt gặt (chọn lọc, không phải tắt hẳn gặt-lại) — chứng minh bằng test thật cả hai nhánh trong cùng một pass.
- Một `fgos-runner --once` chạy song song trong khi một người đang cầm item qua cửa pull `take`: gặt-lại của lượt runner đó không đụng vào claim người, và runner cũng không dispatch lại item đã `doing` — chứng minh bằng e2e qua binary thật (submit → pass-through 2 stage → `take` người → `fgos-runner --once` song song → `return` xanh của người, không lượt nào giẫm lượt nào).
- Vòng đủ của một item runner qua cổng duyệt: submit/add → runner dispatch → `awaiting-approval` → `review` → `approve` → merge → `done`, mang settlement role human, bài học câu-6, và dọn nhánh/worktree đều được assert — chứng minh bằng e2e qua binary + git thật.
- Merge conflict thật trên một main đã rẽ nhánh: sau `approve` bị hủy, cây làm việc NGUYÊN VẸN byte-for-byte (HEAD không đổi, tracked tree sạch, nội dung file không đổi) — chứng minh bằng e2e thật, không chỉ spike.
- Vòng đủ của một item pull-door qua cổng duyệt: `take` → commit → `return` → `review` → `approve` (không bước merge) → `done` — chứng minh bằng e2e qua binary thật.
- `reject` một item pull-door: commit của nó vẫn là lịch sử THẬT trên main sau reject (no-auto-revert) — chứng minh bằng e2e thật.
- Hai việc độc lập (không chung gốc, không phụ thuộc nhau) dispatch trong CÙNG một mẻ đều tới đề xuất, và nhật ký sự kiện sau đó dựng lại đúng nguyên vẹn — chứng minh bằng một cửa sổ chồng-lấn THẬT giữa hai việc (không phải suy luận từ thời gian tường trình, vốn cũng đúng cho hai lần chạy tuần tự trông giống song song).
- Quyền-sở-hữu-gốc dưới hai chủ tranh cùng một gốc: chủ thứ hai luôn bị từ chối nhận, không có cửa sổ nào cả hai cùng nhận được cùng lúc — chứng minh bằng kịch bản đối đầu 2 tác nhân trước khi cell dựng thật, giữ nguyên khi dựng thật.
- Nhập xung đột thật ở tầng con→nhánh-của-gốc VÀ ở tầng gốc→cây chính: cả hai hủy sạch bằng đúng một cơ chế đã chứng minh cho việc-độc-lập trước đây — nhánh/cây nguyên vẹn sau khi hủy, không có tầng nào cần cơ chế riêng.
- Đồng bộ-lại thành công thật (đích đổi không đụng cùng chỗ với việc): việc chuyển thẳng từ đỗ về sẵn sàng nộp lại mà không đi qua "đang làm" — chứng minh bằng kịch bản thật, không rút gọn.
- Đồng bộ-lại gặp xung đột thật (đích đổi đụng đúng chỗ với việc): hủy sạch, việc giữ nguyên đỗ, nhánh của việc không đổi tip — chứng minh bằng kịch bản xung đột thật (không phải một xung đột dựng tắt), cùng cơ chế chứng minh cho cả tầng con→gốc lẫn tầng gốc→cây chính.
- Một câu trả lời làm-rõ của người (`answer`) hoặc một reject/park mang `reason` của người reset ngân sách cổng chống-lặp của chính việc đó — việc dispatch lại thay vì bị đỗ dù đã chạm trần trước đó; một resume trần (không `reason`), một `take` của người (không `answer`/`reason`), và mọi park của chính runner (kể cả mang `reason`) KHÔNG reset — chứng minh bằng test thật per-item cho từng hình, cộng một kịch bản tích hợp `runOnce` thật (RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người cuối cùng của chính việc)).
- Một vòng chỉ-máy-lỗi (không sự kiện người nào) vẫn chết đúng ở trần 3 — reset chỉ xảy ra khi CÓ can thiệp người, không phải mặc định (regression giữ nguyên cùng lúc RUL29 (cổng chống-lặp reset theo can thiệp người cuối cùng của chính việc) được thêm).
- Vòng đủ của một đề xuất nguồn-nhánh từng bị đỗ (chạm trần chống-lặp): người `take` (ghi `branchHeadAtTake`) → commit thêm lên nhánh → `return` đo sạch trên worktree tạm detached tại tip nhánh → `awaiting-approval` mang `branchHeadAtReturn` (không `headAtReturn`) → `review`/`approve` (nguồn đọc là `runner`) → `done` — chứng minh bằng e2e qua binary + git thật (RUL30 (cửa người-hoàn-tất một đề xuất nguồn-nhánh bị đỗ — mở rộng take/return, không verb mới)).
- `return` nguồn-nhánh với nhánh KHÔNG có commit mới kể từ `branchHeadAtTake`: từ chối rõ lý do, việc giữ nguyên `doing`, không đổi tip nhánh — chứng minh bằng test thật.
- `return` nguồn-nhánh trong khi người đang đứng trên chính nhánh `fgw/<id>` đó ở một worktree khác: worktree tạm detached không đụng worktree của người (snapshot trước/sau byte-identical) — chứng minh bằng kịch bản hai-worktree thật, không phải suy luận.

- Đề xuất nguồn runner mở PR qua GitHub (`review --github`) rồi được merge sạch qua `approve --github --pr <n>`: item `done` mang role `human`, cùng khuôn với merge cục bộ — chứng minh bằng test thật qua một `gh` giả tiêm vào tiến trình con thật của CLI (không mock).
- `approve --github` gãy vì lời gọi GitHub thất bại (mọi lý do — xác thực, mạng, giới hạn tần suất, hay chưa rõ): item `blocked` mang lý do cụ thể cộng một bản ghi friction, cùng khuôn `merge-conflict`/`verify-fail-post-merge` — chứng minh bằng test thật.
- `review`/`approve --github` gọi trên một đề xuất KHÔNG phải nguồn runner (pull-door/legacy): từ chối `validation` ngay, không gọi GitHub, đề xuất giữ nguyên trạng thái — chứng minh bằng test thật cho cả hai verb.
- `approve --github` trên một cây làm việc chính đang bẩn (file KHÔNG liên quan đến GitHub còn thay đổi chưa commit): KHÔNG bị chặn bởi phép kiểm cây-sạch của đường cục bộ — phép kiểm đó chỉ áp cho merge cục bộ, không áp cho merge qua GitHub — chứng minh bằng test thật.
- `review --github --pr <n>` trên một PR đã bị đóng KHÔNG merge: nêu đúng số PR, hướng dẫn `fgos reject`, không đổi trạng thái item, không ghi friction — và trả lời trong đúng MỘT lời gọi GitHub dù trường sẵn-sàng-merge của PR đó đọc "chưa rõ" (không chờ-lặp cho phép hỏi thăm này, khác `viewGitHubPRStatus`'s hành vi mặc định) — chứng minh bằng test thật đo số lần gọi GitHub VÀ thời gian chạy.
- `review --github --pr <n>` trên một PR đã merge (kể cả merge thẳng trên GitHub, bỏ qua `approve --github`): chỉ báo tin, không tự đổi trạng thái item cục bộ — chứng minh bằng test thật.
- Một lượt dispatch hỏng vì lý do KHÔNG liên quan tới trợ lý (lỗi worktree, không có output/tier/model) vẫn ghi được một khối vào bản ghi cục bộ, chỉ mang loại lỗi + thông điệp — không throw vì thiếu trường — chứng minh bằng test thật.
- Một việc bị thử lại nhiều lần: mỗi lần thử nối thêm một khối MỚI vào CÙNG bản ghi cục bộ của việc đó, lần thử trước không bị mất — chứng minh bằng test thật.

- Vòng đủ tự-cải-thiện (self-improve loop STR13): một bản ghi friction chưa ngã-ngũ mang từ khóa rủi ro nặng → `evolve` (liệt kê, candidate hiện đủ trường) → `evolve --pick` (đọc-thuần, byte-compare nhật ký trước/sau xác nhận không sự kiện nào bị thêm) → `evolve --submit` (đúng một việc mới, mô tả mang từ khóa) → runner dispatch việc mới đó tới `awaiting-approval` → `review` (source: runner) → `approve` KHÔNG `--acknowledge-iron-law` (item không cha nên target là trunk, và `ironLaw.level` mặc định `ask` — từ chối cứng, nêu tên từ khóa khớp, HEAD không đổi, nhánh còn sống) → `approve --acknowledge-iron-law` (merge, verify xanh, `awaiting-approval → done`, settlement role human, nhánh/worktree dọn sạch) — chứng minh bằng e2e qua binary + git thật, mọi bước tự chạy trong CÙNG file, không dựa vào tham chiếu chéo sang test của cell khác. Hai điều kiện trong ngoặc là điều `0032` làm thành tường minh: cùng diff ấy trên một leaf land vào `fgw/<root>`, hoặc ở `ironLaw.level = "warn"`, không dừng ở bước từ chối.
- `fgos discover <id>` gọi trên một thư mục dự án MỚI, chưa từng có cấu hình runner: không còn chết vì không đọc được cấu hình — cấu hình mặc định được tự viết tại đường mặc định, item đi tiếp vào phán làm-rõ thật (đậu `awaiting-human` khi phán không chắc, đúng fail-safe hiện có, KHÔNG phải một kết quả "thành công" trần trụi) — chứng minh bằng test thật qua binary, PATH của tiến trình phán bị thu hẹp có chủ đích để không gọi trợ lý thật nào trong lúc test. Một `--config` tường minh trỏ đường vắng mặt vẫn báo lỗi ngay như trước, không bao giờ được tự sinh thay (RUL48 (cấu hình runner tự sinh tại đường mặc định khi vắng mặt — không bao giờ đòi người tạo tay trước)).

selected.text:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.

previous.text: - **RUL76 (`execute <executorId> --for <capability>`: the caller states the posture; [ĐÃ BỊ THAY bởi RUL77 (posture thuộc capability; agent executor không khai `for`) — chốt "executor phải khai capability" đã bỏ]; partly reverses the `execute --for` retirement of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch; `execute --for` đã rút), 2026-10-13).** `execute <id>` with no purpose infers the capability from the executor's own `for` list, a required-confinement capability first (`resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints`). RUL70 (executor id theo `providerModel`; gộp `pi`+`codex` thành `openai`) merged `codex` (`for: [code:review, code:debug]`, both `host-write-denied`) and `pi` (no `for`, the writing invocations) into `openai`, so every `execute openai` became write-denied, whatever the work: a documentation task died with `Read-only file system` when Codex tried to refresh its login under bwrap. That rule itself says executors whose `for` differ should not be merged into one entry; the merge kept the codex `for` without noticing pi had none. Instead of splitting the executor, the two-phase `decide`-then-`execute` pattern now carries the purpose to phase two: `execute <id> --for <capability>` runs under that capability's posture. It is accepted only when the executor declares the capability in `for` or the capability's `prefer` names the executor (otherwise `capability-not-served`, before spawning), so config still says which postures an executor accepts; without `--for` the strictest-first inference stays the fail-closed default. `execute --for` with no executor, or combined with `--assignment`/`--contract`, is still refused. `openai.for` gains `execute`, so writing work goes `execute openai --for execute`, which takes the first `cli` invocation (`codex-cli-bypass-fgovn`, unconfined). `--timeout-ms`/`--idle-timeout-ms` override `runner.timeoutMs`/`runner.idleTimeoutMs` per call. Config for a dispatch whose `--cwd` is a worktree with its own `.fgos/config.json` is read from that worktree (5a42bc376, intended), so a branch behind main also resolves older model tiers.
